prs.body:
I bring the audited compiler/runtime work into the 5.0 language-contract release. I make returns leave their enclosing function, run dependency shadows by default, preserve lexical/module identity, and execute synchronous native and VM effects with captured state and tested cleanup. The release contract in `docs/RELEASE_5.0.md` explicitly leaves NanoISA-only self-hosting, complete backend parity, full ownership checking and production isolation unfinished.

I also repair interpreter union-string lifetimes, callback signature identity and VM bridges, private native artifact publication, C++ replay and instrumented wrapper links. Final platform checks found and repaired recursive Bash 3 discovery, long Darwin link closures, shadow-test compiler selection, hermetic MAC dependency tests, obsolete VM exclusions, sanitizer FFI fixture PIC/ODR issues and x86 native array-search argument sequencing. My public compiler version and generated package metadata agree on 5.0.0.

Bounded checks pass 272,403 VM checks, 1,745 translator checks, 1,073 shape checks and all 175 verified/equivalent bytecode programs. VM coverage compiles 244 eligible sources and validates four exclusions. Darwin compiles 187 selected example targets and passes five example regressions. All 27 FFI tests pass normally and with ASan/UBSan using default ODR checking. The x86 array-order failure is reproduced before the fix and passes afterward under both ordinary and coverage builds. The regenerated local release deck and narrative pass all 12 document-pair tests.

The final clean full-suite gate and platform CI remain pending. I keep this PR as a draft until they pass. Earlier checkpoints and their limitations are recorded in `docs/evidence/main-reconciliation-pr334-linux.md` and its linked evidence. The scope review retains floating-point AOT follow-ups and makes stale PR closure conditional on this integration landing and unchanged heads. Finalization ledger: `task_a8786d9cf2c1437fa46c7cfb8b99c30e`.
